tone.note: a colour and nothing else (RFC §7 Q10): fg/mute by default (§7 Q3) or accent/default, which follows the accent axis; emits ll-eyebrow--{tone}. No other tone, no size, no as prop (§7 Q3, Q4, Q7)

children.note: the label: a short string or inline nodes — a category or a counter, never a sentence (§3.4); passed through untouched, the uppercase is CSS

a11y.semanticStructure: Exactly one <span class="ll-eyebrow ll-eyebrow--{tone}"> whose only content is children: no wrapper, no pseudo-element content, no ARIA role, no label, no live region (RFC §3.4, §4.1). Not a heading and carries no heading semantics — the serif title next to it stays the heading. The uppercase is CSS text-transform, so assistive tech reads the author's casing.
a11y.keyboard: Nothing to do: no interactive element, nothing focusable — no a, button, input or tabindex is rendered by the component (RFC §3.3, §4.2). Interactive children are not expected; if the product nests one it keeps its own semantics, product-side.
a11y.decisions: Never inside a heading element: placed before the h2/h3, never inside, so the heading's accessible name stays the title alone (RFC §7 Q9 — a dont guideline; three site usages are restructured at adoption). Nothing is decorative, so nothing is aria-hidden: the label IS the meaning (unlike the Callout's glyph). Contrast is computed by the gate from resolved tokens, never declared here: fg/mute and accent/default on surface/default and on bg/default, under the five accents, at the normal-text threshold (11px is not large text, WCAG 1.4.3). The 0.06em tracking is the type/meta token (§7 Q2), a design arbitration already made — not an accessibility defect to reopen.
a11y.notes: Implemented per RFC §4; this status moves to pass only through the accessibility engine gate, never by assertion.
